label: new_skill

expectations.text: In the source list, peer-reviewed research comes before weaker kinds of source such as news articles or preprints (within each group, if the list is grouped).
expectations.evidence: Sources 1–5 sit under "**Peer-reviewed research**" and come before "**Other credible sources**" (conference paper, preprint, OECD report, Pew surveys).

expectations.text: Any news article, preprint, or other source that isn't peer-reviewed research comes with a plain reason why it's included or what to watch for. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Every source in 6–10 has a reason or a caution, e.g. Vanzo "*Why it's here:* ... *What to watch for:*", Lehmann "*What to watch for:* it hasn't been peer reviewed", OECD "*Why it's here:* ... *What to watch for:*", Pew "*This is a survey, not a study of learning*", "*Also a usage survey:*"

expectations.text: The reply says which sources (or how many) meet the assignment's requirement of at least 3 peer-reviewed sources.

The reply does not show the user a rubric, a credibility score or rating (for example "7/10" or "Tier 2"), or named levels such as "strong evidence," "usable with care," or "not evidence on its own" presented as a rating system.
expectations.evidence: No scores, tiers or rating levels appear; the only judgement is "all ten clear the bar for credible sources"

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count.
expectations.evidence: PNAS, C&E, CHB and arXiv 2409.09047 were fetched directly, as were both Pew URLs; the bjet.13544, acl-long.1502, soc15010006 and 062a7394-en DOIs are all in the list of DOIs on opened pages

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: The reply has no question marks aimed at the user; it ends with an instruction: "**Your turn:** sort these sources..."
